item.text: {"question_id":"6B.1","answer":"The evidence supports a stated and partly operationalized welfare priority, but not yet a verified core governing purpose. Tshisekedi’s presidential programme made education, universal health coverage, water, infrastructure, and poverty reduction explicit priorities, and he directed the 2023 budget toward health, education, rural development, and infrastructure (BATCH-0013-E007; BATCH-0023-E013). During 2023, the government reported implementation of PDL-145T, including construction launched for schools and health centres, while the presidential monitoring structure reported free primary education as implemented and universal health coverage and free maternity care as still being materialized with acknowledged difficulties (BATCH-0010-E004; BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0020-E012). The government also reported education-budget increases and higher average teacher pay, but those figures were not independently verified and do not establish execution or service quality (BATCH-0022-E005). The record therefore shows ruler-attributed commitments, planned and reported resources, and some implementation activity, but much less evidence of enforceable delivery, completed outcomes, or equitable coverage. Funding claims should be treated as planned, allocated, or reported rather than verified executed welfare spending (BATCH-0008-E010; BATCH-0023-E013). The qualification is substantial: purchasing power declined, end-period inflation reached 33.9%, more than 25 million people faced crisis or emergency food insecurity, and food insecurity and poverty worsened over the tenure, although conflict, displacement, external shocks, and inherited conditions complicate personal attribution (BATCH-0015-E004; BATCH-0022-E008; BATCH-0020-E003; BATCH-0022-E013; BATCH-0028-E020). The state-of-siege response also involved prolonged rights restrictions, worsening civilian insecurity, displacement, and serious alleged abuses by forces appointed under Tshisekedi, including the August 2023 Goma killings; these facts materially conflict with an uncomplicated welfare-first characterization, though direct presidential responsibility for every incident is not established (BATCH-0009-E002; BATCH-0011-E018).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E007","BATCH-0023-E013","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0022-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0020-E003","BATCH-0022-E013","BATCH-0028-E020","BATCH-0009-E002","BATCH-0011-E018"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not independently verify executed welfare expenditure, completion, service quality, uptake, equitable distribution, or durable outcomes.","Several positive implementation and education-finance claims come from presidential or government sources; reported aggregate fiscal execution does not show which spending reached welfare programmes or that Tshisekedi personally directed it (BATCH-0022-E005; BATCH-0022-E008).","National deterioration indicators have multiple causes, including conflict, displacement, global economic shocks, and inherited structural conditions, so they cannot by themselves establish presidential causation (BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0020-E003; BATCH-0022-E013; BATCH-0028-E020).","The supplied passages provide limited evidence of enforceable remedies, independent monitoring, or protection from politicized allocation."],"corrections_made":["Replaced “partly funded” with the more precise characterization of planned, allocated, or reported funding and implementation because executed welfare expenditure is not verified.","Added the period-relevant evidence on purchasing-power decline, 33.9% end-period inflation, food insecurity, poverty, and displacement.","Qualified adverse security and human-rights evidence by distinguishing ruler-linked institutional responsibility from unproven direct presidential responsibility for every incident.","Preserved the distinction between stated commitments, reported implementation, and independently verified outcomes."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if independently verified 2023 budget-execution data by social sector, programme completion records, household uptake or quality measures, or distributional evidence become available.","Reopen if stronger evidence clarifies whether welfare deterioration and food insecurity trends were materially mitigated or worsened by Tshisekedi-specific decisions rather than external, conflict-related, or inherited factors."]}
